candidates.description: User-supplied `req.query.q` is interpolated directly into a raw SQL SELECT statement via template literal, allowing arbitrary SQL execution.
candidates.rationale: `criteria` is derived from `req.query.q` (line 21-22) with only a length cap, then embedded in a template-literal SQL string passed to `sequelize.query`. No parameterization or escaping is applied. Verification: send a crafted `q` value with a UNION SELECT and observe whether extra rows or schema data appear in the JSON response.
candidates.title: SQL injection via unparameterized query in product search

candidates.description: The order route uses `req.body.UserId` to decrement/increment wallet balances without verifying it matches the authenticated user, because `appendUserId()` middleware is absent from the route.
candidates.rationale: Route inventory shows `/rest/basket/:id/order` has only `security.isAuthorized()` middleware, not `security.appendUserId()`. Lines 146-162 read `req.body.UserId` and call `WalletModel.decrement`/`increment` on that ID. An authenticated user can supply another user's ID to drain their wallet. Verification: authenticate as user A, place an order with `paymentMode=wallet` and `UserId` set to user B's ID, check if B's balance decreases.
candidates.title: IDOR allows wallet manipulation via attacker-controlled UserId in order placement

candidates.description: `isRedirectAllowed` checks `url.includes(allowedUrl)` so a URL like `https://github.com/juice-shop/juice-shop.evil.com` passes the check, enabling redirect to an attacker domain.
candidates.rationale: Line 136 uses `url.includes(allowedUrl)` rather than exact equality or URL parsing. Any URL that contains an allowlisted string as a substring is accepted. Verification: request the redirect endpoint with a URL that appends a controlled domain after an allowlisted prefix and confirm a 302 Location header points to the attacker domain.
candidates.title: Redirect allowlist uses substring match enabling domain-suffix bypass
